chapter: After the Army: JATP, clubs and first Europe trips
title: Sightseeing in Europe: Joan of Arc, Carcassonne, Stonehenge
summary: He enthuses over historic sites such as Joan of Arc's, Carcassonne and Stonehenge.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, going to Europe now is

like going to Newark, New Jersey. Because everybody has been there and actually some of them have been there too many times. Another thing I liked, I never could get over these old places like that we had read about. For instance, where they burned Joan of Arc, that's still beautiful. They've got it you know, all fixed up, but it's the same spot.
And we saw where she was kept captive for so long. And we saw so many old castles.

Yes, Carcassonne). The old city of Carcassonne). It's still preserved. And all around it at the bottom of the hill is the modern Carcassonne. But Carcassonne) is a where they have dungeons and torture chambers. Moats, still there.
That must be one of the best preserved medieval towns that there are.
I think it is. But I also was glad to see Stone Henge. Yes I'll never get over seeing Stone Henge for the first time.
That's hard to believe isn't it?

stones. Where they got them from and the distance they had to take them, it must have taken them a long time. And they are so exact. It's so exact. One ray of light comes through there and hits a certain spot and they could tell what day.....
Yes, midsummer's day or something like that.
Yes. That's really amazing. Things like that is why I always wanted to go to Europe. And every Country has got something that's different. Something there is different.
